transcripts.transcript: Think of a student who can follow a recipe perfectly but becomes unsure when one ingredient is missing. Knowing the steps is useful, but understanding why each step matters makes adaptation possible. I mention this because the same distinction applies to laboratory work: a procedure should not be learned as an unexplained sequence of actions.

transcripts.transcript: We have doubled the number of online resources, yet students still report difficulty finding the right material. transcripts.transcript: The speakers were well prepared, and the topics attracted considerable interest. Still, several participants had to leave before they could ask questions.
